method.ray_method: MuJoCo CPU mj_ray first-hit; optical Z from normalized pinhole ray
method.obstacle_ge_025_definition: First visible nonfloor surface hit at least .025 m above simulator floor; surface-point stratum, not object-instance-size coverage
method.ply_provenance: All actual obstacle PLY vertices exactly recovered as unchanged measured frame/pixel first observation per .03m voxel; ground truth assigned by source-camera ray, never by drifted map Z

limitations: Ten frozen held-out frames sampled regularly every8pixels; not all visible area, confidence interval or object-instance recall.
Floor recall includes uncertain/obstacle labels in ALL valid visible floor denominator. Separate completeness also includes visible floor without valid measured depth.
Only first visible scene geometry is scored; occluded/unobserved objects and floor are not counted. No truth/depth-agreement filtering removes difficult valid samples.
Obstacle>=2.5cm is hit-height stratum; near-threshold object instances may be absent. Synthetic low-obstacle tests remain separate.
PLY leakage scores every actual retained obstacle vertex by its source pixel physical visibility; it does not measure map registration/seams or classify world Z.
No navigation quality or accepted clean-map claim.

floor_height_causal_scoring.method: Same physical wheel/IMU+mount classification coordinate frame and original rays; compare measured-depth height to evaluator-only optical-Z height. No reclassification or modified depth.

support_and_classifier_diagnosis.method: Unchanged full measured prediction/correction/support reconstructed byte-identically; branch scoring only. Evaluator CPU ToF first-hit geometry remains diagnostic-only.
support_and_classifier_diagnosis.integration_hypothesis: Sensor hist_data mean/sigma describe closest significant depth cluster, not whole-zone depth statistics. Yet local mean anchoring and sloping_zone_support compare a full projected zone prediction/distribution with that selected-cluster statistic. On a continuously sloping physical floor, selected near rays are not representative of far rays in the same zone; a short/flattened predicted patch can agree with the selected mean while physical floor becomes apparent raised geometry.
